we have shown that IL-1Ra is produced by BM cells in vivo, that it is released into the circulation and that it can be taken up by non-BM cells and exert its anti-inflammatory effect on the vessel wall.

the IL-1RA gene expression in the bone marrow and non-bone-marrow cells, and IL-1RA protein production in bone marrow and nonbone marrow-derived cells, are important factors to suppress neointimal formation and arterial inflammation after vascular injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-1Ra can be produced by both bone marrowderived and non-bone-marrow-derived cells.
the IL-1Ra originating from the BMDCs is more potent than IL-1Ra derived from the non-BMDCs in the suppression of neointimal formation in the arterial injury model.
